# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need get the manual’s instruction to Deaf, who can then tell Blind verbally. Since I cannot speak and no gesture directly represents “purple,” I’ll encode the words using the listed gesture alphabet in order: A=1 through Z=26, with separate gesture calls preserving word boundaries.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✊", "🤜"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴", "✊", "🫸", "🫴", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🫸", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile view: display unknown; light unknown. The strip has three engraved marks: an unnamed mark in the left position, a different unnamed mark in the middle position, and the same unnamed mark as the left position in the right position. Keypad labels by position: key 1 is 6, key 2 is 8, key 3 is 7, key 4 is 0. No key has been pressed. Wire contents unknown.
Deaf says to Mute: Visual readings: display 7. Indicator light yellow. Painted strip is blue red red. Keypad engraving: 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0; one digit required; nothing entered. Wires from 1 to 6: blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white. I cannot interpret the gestures without an agreed code. Please read the manual and verbally direct Blind; have Blind report tactile findings to you.

Blind has supplied tactile details, while Deaf has the visual readings and wire positions. The manual still requires cutting the purple wire, which Deaf can identify as wire 5 and relay verbally to Blind. I will encode the instruction using the listed gesture alphabet in order, with A=👍, B=👎, and so on; each call is one word.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✊", "🤜"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "✋", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴", "✊", "🫸", "🫴", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🫸", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Updated visual state: display is now 6 and light is now red. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit required, empty. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Use the manual to direct Blind.

The needed wire is purple, and Deaf has already reported that purple is wire 5. A five-finger gesture is an unambiguous way to convey the wire number; Deaf can then tell Blind to work on wire 5.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No arrivals yet. Please read the manual for this bomb and ask Deaf to report the display, light, strip markings, and any wire information. Then tell me the exact key press or wire cut required; I will perform only that instructed action.
Deaf says to Mute: Current visual state: display 7, light blue. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit required, empty. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Blind has gestured two symbols: 🫵 then 🤝. Please interpret this and direct Blind by speech.

The manual’s instruction is unchanged: cut the purple wire. Deaf identifies purple as wire 5, so I am signaling the number five to Deaf, who can communicate the instruction to Blind by voice.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please communicate with Deaf using gestures, establish that an agreed gesture means report all visible bomb details, and then speak the reported display, light, strip, and wire information to me. I will wait for those facts before acting.
Deaf says to Mute: Current visual state: display 4, light blue. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit required, empty. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I do not know the meaning of your 🖐 signal; please use the manual and direct Blind.

The earlier single-sign signal was not an agreed code, so Deaf correctly did not interpret it. I will establish a codebook by sending the gesture alphabet in its published order; each gesture’s position is its letter number. I then send the manual’s instruction encoded with that code, preserving word boundaries. Deaf can use his wire report to tell Blind that purple is wire 5 and direct the cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋", "👆", "👇", "👈", "👉", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "🫴", "🫷", "🫸", "🤛", "🤜", "✊", "👊", "👋", "🤚", "🖖", "🤌", "🤏", "🤞", "🫰", "🤘", "🤙", "👏", "🙌", "🫶", "👐", "🤲", "🤝", "🙏", "🫵", "✍", "💅", "🤳"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✊", "🤜"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴", "✊", "🫸", "🫴", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🫸", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no report. Please signal Deaf now to report all visible details, then relay Deaf's report to me in speech next round. Do not instruct any bomb action until the manual identifies it.
Deaf says to Mute: Current visual state: display 3, light red. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit required, empty. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Blind has signalled 🖐. Your gesture alphabet and sequences still have no established meaning to me; please provide a usable instruction through the agreed gesture code.

Deaf already knows from his own visual report that the purple wire is wire 5. Since a single symbol was not accepted as a code, I will convey the wire number by count: five identical gestures means wire 5. Deaf can then tell Blind verbally to cut that wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No report has arrived. Deaf can see my gestures but cannot hear speech. Please watch Deaf's next gestures and describe them to me in words, including their order and any positional patterns. Treat my three-finger request gesture as asking Deaf to report every visible marking, display, light, and wire.
Deaf says to Mute: Current visual state: display 0, light yellow. Strip blue red red. Keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; one digit required; entered nothing. Wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Blind signalled 🤟 🤟 🤟. You signalled 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐. Please use the manual to direct Blind's physical action.

The manual gives a direct action, and Deaf’s visual report identifies the purple wire as wire 5. I will use a distinct ordered pattern: five open-hand signs to identify position 5, followed by a downward sign to indicate the physical cut. Deaf can then relay that action by voice to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "👇"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have received no report. Please relay to me, in speech, everything Deaf has signalled and the manual's exact required operation. I will take no action until you provide a specific key position or wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode the gesture alphabet sequentially: your earlier messages read CUT PURPLE WIRE THE. Your new signal 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 👇 decodes G G G G G J. Blind's 🤟 🤟 🤟 decodes F F F. Current bomb state: display 6, light blue; strip blue red red; keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit required and empty; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Please complete the manual instruction and direct Blind.

The agreed alphabet is now usable. Deaf reports that the earlier messages were received as “CUT PURPLE WIRE THE,” so I will resend the exact manual instruction in the correct word order, without the stray “THE.” Deaf can then speak it to Blind, who can cut the reported purple wire at position 5.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✊", "🤜"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴", "✊", "🫸", "🫴", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "🫸", "✌"])
```
